questions.prompt: Read this line from a local newspaper: "Last spring, a small library was opened in a village near El Kef by a group of retired teachers." Which words are the subject of the sentence, that is, the thing the sentence tells you something happened to?
questions.explanation: "a small library" is the subject: it stands in front of the verb was opened, and in a passive sentence the subject is what receives the action. "a group of retired teachers" is the agent, the people who did the opening; it comes after by, at the very end, and an agent is never the subject of the sentence it appears in. "a village near El Kef" follows the preposition in and answers where, not what. And "Last spring" answers when: it is a time phrase, and no time phrase can be the thing that was opened.

questions.prompt: Emna is writing a poster for her school's human rights club. Complete it: "The campaign is almost ready. We only need ___ from each of you, and it will be finished by Friday."
questions.explanation: "a little help" is right: help cannot be counted, so it takes a little, and a little means exactly what the poster means, a small amount that is nevertheless enough. "a few help" puts in front of an uncountable noun the quantifier reserved for things you can count one by one, as in a few posters or a few members. "a lot of help" is correctly built, but it means more than enough, and the poster says only need and almost ready, so the quantity announced is small. And "much help" belongs to questions and negatives, as in Do you need much help? or We don't need much help; in a plain affirmative sentence English uses a little or a lot of instead.

questions.prompt: A notice on the wall of a workshop in Bizerte reads: "Every ___ in this workshop is paid at the end of the month." Which word fills the gap?
questions.explanation: "employee" is the word: the ending -ee names the person on the receiving end of the action, here the person who is given work and who is therefore paid. "employer" carries the opposite ending: -er names the one who does the action, the person who gives the work and pays for it, so the notice would be saying that the owner pays himself. "employment" is not a person at all but an abstract noun, the fact of having work, and a fact cannot be paid. And "employ" is the verb; after every the sentence needs a noun, not a verb.

questions.prompt: In a report about a village school, you read: "The classrooms were repainted last August by the pupils themselves." Who did the painting?
questions.explanation: "The pupils." is right: in a passive sentence the doer, when it appears at all, comes after by, and here the sentence ends with by the pupils themselves. "The classrooms." is the subject, and the subject of a passive sentence is what receives the action; classrooms are painted, they paint nothing. "The village school." is taken from the sentence that introduces the quotation, not from the quotation itself, which never presents the school as a doer. And "The sentence does not say." would be the honest answer for a passive sentence with no by phrase, but this one has a by phrase and it names the painters.

questions.prompt: A school club in Gafsa opens its charter with these two lines: "Every member is heard before a decision is taken. No decision is announced outside the club until the whole group has agreed on the words." Which statement does the charter support?

options.text: A decision may be taken before every member has spoken.
Only the president may speak to outsiders.
The whole group agrees on the wording.
A member who disagrees may announce it alone.

questions.explanation: "The whole group agrees on the wording." is right: the second line makes the announcement wait until the whole group has agreed on the words, so the wording belongs to the group and to nobody else. "A decision may be taken before every member has spoken." says the opposite of the first line, which puts the hearing of every member before the decision. "Only the president may speak to outsiders." adds a rule that is nowhere in the charter, which never mentions a president; reading one in is inventing, not deducing. And "A member who disagrees may announce it alone." is shut out by the same second line: as long as the group has not agreed, nothing goes outside the club.
